Array.from().description:
ES2015
Array.from(arrayLike[, mapFn[, thisArg]]);
return a new Array instance, shallow-copied from an array-like or iterable object, optionally mapping each element through mapFn.
The mapFn part is optional — select and delete it for the plain `Array.from(arrayLike)` form.

Array.prototype.at().description:
ES2022
const item = items.at(index);
The `at()` method takes an integer value and returns the item at that index, allowing for positive and negative integers. Negative integers count back from the last item in the array.
Returns `undefined` if the given index can not be found.

Array.prototype.concat().description:
let newArray = oldArray.concat([value1[, value2[, ...[, valueN]]]]);
return a new array

Array.prototype.every().description:
ES5
array.every(callbackFn(element[, index[, array]])[, thisArg]);
return 'true' if the callback function returns a truthy value for every array element. Otherwise, 'false'.
returns 'true' for any condition put on an empty array

Array.prototype.findIndex().description:
ES2015
array.findIndex(callbackFn(element[, index[, array]])[, thisArg]);
return the index of the first element in the array that satisfies the provided testing function. Otherwise, it returns '-1'.
6th edition

Array.prototype.forEach(function(current.description:
ES5
array.forEach(function callbackFn(currentValue [, index [, array]]) { }[, thisArg]);

Array.prototype.join().description:
array.join([separator]);
return a string with all array elements joined. If array.length is 0, the empty string is returned.

Array.prototype.pop().description:
array.pop();
return the removed element from the array; 'undefined' if the array is empty.

Array.prototype.push().description:
arr.push(element1[, ...[, elementN]]);
return the new length of the array.

Array.prototype.shift().description:
array.shift();
return the removed element from the array; 'undefined' if the array is empty.

Array.prototype.slice().description:
array.slice([begin[, end]]);
 return a shallow copy of a portion of an array into a new array object selected from begin to end (end not included). The original array will not be modified.

Array.prototype.some().description:
ES5
array.some(callbackFn(element[, index[, array]])[, thisArg]);
return 'true' if the callback function returns a truthy value for at least one element in the array. Otherwise, 'false'.
returns false for any condition put on an empty array.

Array.prototype.sort().description:
array.sort([compareFunction(firstEl, secondEl)]);
return the sorted array. Note that the array is sorted in-place, and no copy is made.

Array.prototype.unshift().description:
array.unshift(element1[, ...[, elementN]])();
return the new length of the array.
